office_does: The Pierce County Auditor is the nonpartisan official who runs county elections and handles document recording, licensing, marriage licenses and passport acceptance.
race_blurb: One-term incumbent Linda Farmer, a former Lakewood councilmember, faces Damon Townsend, a former Pierce County elections supervisor and Cascade Party board member. The race turns on election-administration credentials, office performance measures and party ties.

candidates.summary: Pierce County Auditor since her 2022 election, previously a Lakewood councilmember and communications executive, running on election security, voter access and customer service.
highlights: Says her first term added more ballot drop boxes, two new vote centers and expanded voter outreach [S6]
Earned the CERA elections-administration credential in 2025 and co-chairs the VoteWA executive steering committee [S2]
Runs on easy-to-navigate service for car tabs, passports, recording and marriage licenses [S3][S6]
Endorsed by 25 other Washington county auditors, County Executive Ryan Mello and Pierce County Democrats [S4]

experience.basis: One-term incumbent with prior city council and charter review service who runs on her first-term record and 'two decades of public service and executive management experience'.

candidates.summary: Former Pierce County Elections Supervisor (2014-2019) and telecommunications operations manager, running on modernized systems, public performance dashboards and low-cost service.
highlights: Pierce County Elections Supervisor 2014-2019 and interim elections manager in Clallam and Cowlitz counties in 2020 [S1]
Says he helped build the county's modern tabulation system and ballot-tracking procedures still in use [S7]
Proposes public dashboards on processing times, signature acceptance and licensing waits, and process-driven cost cuts [S1]
Cascade Party board member; started a Peninsula County exploratory committee in 2026 [S1]
Endorsed by Mainstream Republicans of Washington, the Tacoma-Pierce County REALTORS, IAFF Local 31 and AFSCME Council 2/Local 120 [S3]

spending.basis: Proposes performance dashboards, open data and process-driven cost reduction, and pledges service 'at the lowest burden to taxpayers' with 'fiscal responsibility'; scoped to the office's own operations.

experience.basis: Challenger who has never held elected office and says office should not be about 'political ambition', though he cites five years running the county's elections and statewide election-system work.

reform.basis: Sits on the board of a third party and discloses that membership rather than claiming nonpartisanship; states no position on PAC money, term limits or other reform markers.
